major_concerns: Oracle incompleteness for semantic failures may bias results
Emulator-device fidelity vs. real hardware not fully addressed
Validator design is a major intervention and may confound attribution to the LLM
Risk of overfitting validator/repair prompts to the task set
Potential for LLM/provider drift across runs
required_design_repairs: Precisely specify oracle coverage and include human spot-checks for oracle disagreements
Publish validator rule-set and repair prompts; preregister them
Include sensitivity analysis varying validator strictness and repair prompt phrasing
Log model-version, timestamps, and hashes to detect provider drift; freeze model identifier if possible
Define and report exclusions and retry-policy clearly

major_concerns: Latency/cost estimates are highly sensitive to provider variability and rate limits
Single-provider measurement risks non-generalizable conclusions
Tail latency from rare multi-iteration repairs can dominate viability metrics
Timing measured in emulation may not reflect integrated deployment latencies
required_design_repairs: Measure across multiple providers/endpoints or simulate provider variability
Include rate-limit/backoff modeling and document API variability handling
Report full latency distributions, emphasize tail behavior, and perform sensitivity to max repair iterations
Preregister cost-calculation method and provider pricing snapshot; snapshot model versions

major_concerns: Licensing and redistribution of vendor images may block artifact release
Defining comprehensive machine-verifiable oracles for complex behaviors is hard and may miss important failure modes
Risk of benchmark being gamed / overfitting to oracle specifics
Engineering effort to produce and validate reproducible emulation may exceed available runtime budget
required_design_repairs: Specify licensing plan and provide minimal, fully open-device images or synthetic models to avoid IP issues
Define oracle scope explicitly and include a documented human-audit protocol for oracle disagreements
Provide artifact integrity checks, simple reproduction quickstart, and CI-style reproducibility tests
Document known oracle blind spots and recommend how third parties can extend or verify them

major_concerns: Multiple comparisons risk across prompt templates, seeds, and complexity levels
Template design may bias outputs and reduce generalizability
Choice of reproducibility metrics (e.g., edit-distance vs. oracle pass) may affect conclusions
required_design_repairs: Preregister templates and justify their design; include examples
Apply multiple-comparison corrections and report effect sizes with CIs
Report both syntactic/semantic metrics and illustrative failure exemplars to contextualize numeric results
Include model-version locking and seed logs to ensure reproducibility

major_concerns: Defining 'unsafe' and 'irreversible' states requires careful operationalization to avoid subjective labeling
Agent orchestration bugs could masquerade as safety failures if not instrumented
Simulated rollback behavior may not reflect complexities of real systems (state, side-effects)
Bounded-agent policies (whitelists) may be overconservative and reduce utility
required_design_repairs: Provide precise, operational definitions and checklists for unsafe/irreversible outcomes
Instrument agent harness heavily and include unit tests to separate orchestration bugs from agent logic failures
Simulate a variety of rollback semantics and include human-reviewed ground truth for ambiguous cases
Report utility trade-offs (blocked safe actions) alongside safety metrics and preregister whitelist/validator rules
